To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we introduce RLgraph: Flexible Computed Graphs for Deep RL, a library for implementing and executing high performance deep reinforcement learning algorithms, and that RLgraph is flexible and extensible, and achieves high performance in different deep learning frameworks.

1) RLgraph enables a flexible, high-performance framework for designing and executing RL algorithms, 2) RLgraph is able to achieve performance comparable to state-of-the-art implementations of RL algorithms in PyTorch and TensorFlow.

RLgraph provides a framework for defining and executing flexible computation graphs that can be executed on a variety of deep learning frameworks, including TensorFlow, PyTorch, and MXNet, and on a variety of distributed backends, including Horovod, Ray, and Dask.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (1) A flexible and extensible library for designing and implementing RL algorithms.

(1) the development of a high-level language for composing RL algorithms, (2) a graph-based execution engine for distributed and parallel execution, and (3) the development of RL algorithms and benchmarks to demonstrate the utility of the library.
the design of a flexible, high performance, and extensible framework that allows researchers to focus on the core RL algorithms and not be concerned with implementation and execution details.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RLgraph is a library for designing flexible computation graphs for deep reinforcement learning.
RLgraph is the first library that allows for flexible composition of deep RL components in a unified way and that allows the user to execute the resulting graph in different backends.
RLgraph is a library for designing flexible and high-performance computation graphs for deep reinforcement learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a library to define and execute RL graphs.
we have built a library for designing RL agents and algorithms in a flexible and composable way, which can run on different deep learning frameworks, and distributed backends.

we have developed a framework for building and executing RL algorithms that are flexible in the sense that they can work on different hardware and software backends and are also flexible in the sense of being able to support a wide range of algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the logical structure of a reinforcement learning algorithm can be cleanly separated from the backend implementation, allowing for a more flexible, extensible, and efficient framework for developing and executing RL algorithms.
the separation of logical and physical computation graphs allows for the creation of high-level RL algorithms with low implementation and execution complexity.
the separation of logical and physical graphs enables a high level of flexibility in the design, execution, and testing of RL agents.
